ambiguities.observation: §2.1 constrains display_fps>=30 and physics_hz=60. The default mock configuration (numpy XPBD + PIL rasteriser + 1080p synthetic camera) reports lower framework counters; with the optional engine backends the same 300-frame loop reaches 25.5 fps / p95 44.5 ms. Both sets are local-host numbers, archived under local_benchmarks; per-step numbers are reproduced by scripts/bench_engines.py and the 300-frame loop by scripts/bench_e2e.py. The §17.10 target-hardware table remains entirely TODO.
ambiguities.question: Does §2.1's fps constraint apply to mock framework counters, or only to target-hardware measurements?
ambiguities.ruling: §2.1 constrains the shipped product on target hardware. Mock framework counters and local-host benchmarks are engineering evidence only: they are never written into the §17.10 table, never reported as a product guarantee, and §1.3's five fps meters stay independent. Consequence: (a) no mock-derived number may be presented as meeting or missing §2.1; (b) the ≤100 ms p95 bound is still checked against the mock loop because it is a latency budget that the loop can genuinely violate, and it now passes with 55% headroom.

ambiguities.observation: A 300-frame mock run reports commits=0 and material_histogram all AI_PRIOR; COMMIT / DEGRADE are covered by unit + integration tests, and a 60-frame known-Θ* synthetic trajectory verifies ε_Θ decreases.
ambiguities.question: Must the 300-frame mock main loop itself reach a COMMIT, or is gate-level plus synthetic-trajectory coverage sufficient for Phase 3?
ambiguities.ruling: Gate-level plus synthetic-trajectory coverage is sufficient. COMMIT depends on human excitation (pull / release energy decay) that a scripted scene cannot honestly reproduce; forcing a commit would require fabricating observations. Phase 3 acceptance therefore stands on: three-gate unit tests, a known-Θ* trajectory whose ε_Θ decreases, and the end-to-end wiring test that a BATCH reaching the gates does version the asset.

ambiguities.observation: Pipeline C uses a multiprocessing worker; calibration_results varies between identical 300-frame runs because submission timing is wall-clock dependent. Physics/framing are deterministic when calibration is disabled (regression test).
ambiguities.question: Is wall-clock-dependent submission count acceptable, or must the mock worker be synchronised for reproducible acceptance runs?
ambiguities.ruling: Wall-clock-dependent submission is accepted, because the binding requirement is that pipeline C never blocks pipeline B (met: separate process, bounded queue, terminate-on-exit). Determinism is guaranteed only with pipeline C disabled, and that mode is now the documented contract for benchmarks and acceptance runs (`--no-calibration`, used by scripts/bench_engines.py and the README A/B command).

deviations.description: SPEC mandates 12 test files; the tree has 15. The 12 §16 files are unchanged; test_json_safety.py, test_make_runner.py and test_engine_adapters.py are additional regression files (strict-JSON fix, Windows-runner fix, P0-P4 engine adapters). The SPEC count was not edited.

configs/default.yaml adds engine-backend keys introduced by the P0-P4 adapters: physics.self_collision[_radius_m], perception.{body_backend,hand_backend,body_depth_m,hand_depth_m}, render.backend opencv value, keyframe.fashn_* client keys, calibration.grad_backend (fd|warp), asset.geometry silhouette value. All are consumed by the adapters that read them; no second threshold copy exists (§0.2).

SimReadyMesh gained an optional `seams` array (vertex pairs joined by near-rigid distance constraints). Physics still receives one mesh built by the unchanged builders; seams are pattern data, not topology, so D13 asset separation and the repair gates are unaffected. MeshRepairer now copies `seams` through (it previously rebuilt the mesh and silently dropped them).

Extra files not listed in §4: .gitignore, .gitattributes, STRUCTURED_REPORT.json, PRODUCT.md, scripts/make.py, scripts/bench_engines.py, make.cmd, the extra regression tests, configs/local.example.yaml, var/logs/run.jsonl, assets/samples/garment.png, the P0-P4 engine modules physics/warp_solver.py, render/cv2_render.py, calibration/warp_grad.py, the texturing modules asset/uv.py and render/texture.py, and the web shell app/serve.py. All are documentation/build/data/engine/product artefacts required for a working delivery; no §4 file is missing.

configs/default.yaml carries extra keys (g1_iou_threshold, g2, confidence_weights, mesh_resolution, etc.) defined by §7/§10. The unused N/m keys support_stiffness / attach_stiffness were replaced by the actually consumed dimensionless support_relax / attach_relax (§0.2).

Two number tables now coexist and MUST NOT be conflated. (1) The §17.10 target-hardware measured table in README stays entirely TODO. (2) A separate '本机实测基准' section reports local-host engine numbers (RTX 5060 Laptop 8 GB, warp-lang 1.19, CUDA 13.4) produced by scripts/bench_engines.py and archived under var/eval/bench.json; those are engineering evidence about the optional backends, not a claim about the target hardware. measured_numbers stays empty because it is reserved for the §17.10 table.

The 'no GPU / no weights / no network' guarantee holds for the DEFAULT mock configuration. factory.build honours explicit engine selection in every mode, so `--physics-solver warp` or `render.backend: opencv` will initialise CUDA (or CPU kernels) and read local packages in mock mode too. README states this boundary explicitly; no weights or network access is ever added by the engine backends.

risks: Every real adapter still falls back to Stub with E_ADAPTER_FALLBACK when its optional dependency or credential is missing; the P0 engine backends (warp, opencv) are the only new paths exercised locally, and the P1 MediaPipe path had no mediapipe install on the build host (fallback-only coverage there).
Pipeline C submission count is wall-clock dependent (ruling A3: accepted; determinism is provided by --no-calibration).
The §17.10 target-hardware table stays empty; local-host engine benchmarks exist and are labelled as such (deviations), never as target-hardware results.

FASHN keyframe generation sends the user's camera frame and garment image to a third-party HTTP service; it is opt-in (mode real/hybrid + keyframe.backend + FASHN_API_KEY) and no privacy guarantee is implied.
Self-collision is vertex-level hash-grid repulsion behind physics.self_collision (default false); point-triangle collision and cloth self-contact resolution remain unimplemented.
Warp physics measures 5.27 ms/step at the 5936-vertex budget point: 3.2x inside the 60 Hz requirement but ~5% above the SPEC §8 '<=5 ms @ N=6000' figure. numpy is 66 ms/step at the same size.

MediaPipe trackers use the legacy Solutions API (mp.solutions.*) whose lifetime is not guaranteed across major versions; a future removal surfaces as E_ADAPTER_FALLBACK rather than a crash, but the real path would degrade to Stub.

app/serve.py is a local development preview: Flask's built-in server, bound to 127.0.0.1, with no auth/TLS/rate limits. Exposing it beyond localhost requires a production WSGI server plus an authenticating reverse proxy; the UI/API contract is not yet hardened for multi-tenant SaaS.

The current XPBD contact path has no formal non-penetration guarantee like OGC/IPC: it projects end-point penetrations and clamps per-substep displacement. DAT is available only inside the optional Newton backend; OGC and pyuipc are not integrated, so a formal guarantee on the default path would require further work.

The optional Newton VBD backend is experimental: its soft contacts still report residual penetration (4/480 and 24/1560 after 20 steps), the first run compiles Warp kernels for 1-2 minutes, and its energy numbers are not comparable with XPBD. The default XPBD path is unchanged.

fixed_defects: Energy-budget contraction used a 40-step bisection that called elastic_energy 43 times per step (~85% of the step at 5936 vertices); replaced with a cached, preallocated quadratic-form search while keeping the float64 exact re-check and the §7 invariant.
The Warp step allocated ~10 device arrays per step and launched a redundant zero-delta kernel per iteration; replaced with persistent buffers and an apply-and-zero kernel.
Per-step validation lives in tests/test_engine_adapters.py (contract_scale budget + monotonicity, step-time guard).
